name: Nauna
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 6 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Blust, Robert. 2021. Sketch 8: Nauna. In Eight Languages of the Admiralty Islands, Papua New Guinea, 547-622. Language & Linguistics in Melanesia Special Issue 2021 (ISSN 0023-1959). Port Moresby: Linguistic Society of Papua New Guinea.
catalog_locator: sec. 8.2 Phonology, pp. 550-551 (last paragraph of 8.2, straddling the 550/551 page break; pp. 5-6 of the 77-page sketch file)
catalog_quote: Stress was rarely recorded in Nauna. Where it was written it is generally penultimate, but occasionally final, as in [saŋahúl] ‘ten’. Since little evidence of suprasegmental contrast was noticed in nine and one half hours of contact with the speaker, it is assumed on the basis of the data collected that stress is not phonemic.
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: header 'LLM SPECIAL ISSUE 2021.. Sketch 8: NAUNA, Robert Blust'). The quoted passage is at the text layerstraddling the printed page break 550/551 at the end of sec. 8.2 PHONOLOGY, word for word: 'Stress was rarely recorded in Nauna. Where it was written it is generally penultimate, but occasionally final, as in [saŋahúl] 'ten'. Since little evidence of suprasegmental contrast was noticed in nine and one half hours of contact with the speaker, it is assumed on the basis of the data collected that stress is not phonemic.' It is immediately followed by '8.3. GRAMMAR', so the locator (sec. 8.2, pp. 550-551) is exact. I read the whole of 8.1-8.2 (pp. 547-551): phoneme table, consonant and vowel…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is non-contrastive and, where noted, falls on the penultimate syllable, with occasional final stress (e.g. saŋahúl 'ten'); the author explicitly flags that stress was seldom transcribed and the generalization rests on 9.5 hours with one speaker.
new_statements.exceptions: Occasional final stress, example [saŋahúl] 'ten'; no conditioning stated. Vowel length marginally phonemic for /a/ in three words (ma:tu, mwa:ni, kaka:ro) but no link to stress is drawn.
new_statements.domain_note: Isolated elicited words (modified Swadesh list + grammatical items) from a single 15-year-old speaker of Paramoh village, March 1975; statement is tentative by the author's own wording ('rarely recorded', 'assumed').
new_statements.identity_note: Source describes the speech of Paramoh village, the single Nauna-speaking village on Nauna island (one speaker, Puliokai Kiendaman, recorded in Lorengau 1975); this is naun1237 itself, no dialect split reported.
